rappel_detail.notes: First of 1-3 rappels down the upper ice step (up to 300+ ft of AI3 alpine ice); V-thread anchors leave no gear behind and are not left in place between ascent and descent.
Continue down the upper ice step; belay to easier ground climber's-left/east into the chute rather than committing to team-arrest on exposed ice.
First of 1-2 rappels down the lower ice step, same anchor style as above.
Final rappel through the lower ice step; after the chute, move fast across the traverse back toward the Rock Step since this stretch sits under the active Kautz Ice Cliff.

set.rappels: 2-5 rappels through the Kautz ice steps on the way down, depending on conditions and how much rope you carry: 1-3 down the upper ice step and 1-2 down the lower one, all on ice anchors you build yourself. The four stations listed are a middle count for a party on a single 60 m rope; with two 60 m ropes it can be as few as two, plus some downclimbing.
set.rappel_count_note: The count ranges from 2-5 rappels total, depending on rope length/number of ropes carried: 1-3 on the upper ice step, 1-2 on the lower ice step. 4 is used here as a representative middle count for a party on a single 60m rope; fewer with two ropes, more if short-pitching. With two 60 m ropes, two double-rope rappels plus some downclimbing get most parties through the steepest ice.
